title: SI-4: The lock records the holder's pid and a random id made once at process start, and the holder refreshes the loc
description:
Owning doc: docs/research/service-interface.md#11-plan (SI-4).

The lock records the holder's pid and a random id made once at process start, and the holder refreshes the lock file's mtime every 10 s. A lock with this process's id is refused (a second acquire in one process). A lock whose pid is alive in this namespace and is not this process is refused, as today. In app mode a lock whose pid is dead is taken at once, as today. Otherwise (the pid is this process's with a foreign id, or in server mode the pid is not visible) the lock is taken only once its mtime is older than 30 s. The same holds for each call's log writer

Why: A container restarts with Bun as pid 1 every time, and two containers can share one volume (section 9)
Today: missing: `src/core/log/writer.ts:131-138`
acceptance_criteria: A test writes a lock holding `process.pid`, a foreign id and a 60 s old mtime and starts the app: it takes the lock. The same lock with a fresh mtime is refused, then taken once 30 s pass. A second acquire inside the same process is still refused, and so is a lock held by another live process. A two-container test on one volume: the second container stays refused while the first runs, and takes the lock within 40 s of the first being killed with `SIGKILL`. Positive control: today's `acquireLock` fails the first case, and the pid-and-id rule without the mtime check fails the two-container case

title: SV-E7: Address rules for callback URLs: `http` and `https` only, no redirects followed
description:
Owning doc: docs/ux/SERVER.md#6-events-and-webhooks (SV-E7).

Address rules for callback URLs: `http` and `https` only, no redirects followed. RFC 1918, unique-local and loopback addresses are allowed, because a self-hosted client on the same box or the same LAN is the normal case and the per-key host allowlist of SV-K4 is the real guard. Link-local and metadata ranges, `169.254.0.0/16` and `fe80::/10`, are refused at submit time and again at delivery time after DNS resolution, so a name that resolves there after submit is still refused

From: Standard Webhooks security section; a key holder must not reach the box's metadata service
Today: missing
acceptance_criteria: A callback to `http://169.254.169.254/` gets 422 at submit; a hostname that resolves to `169.254.1.1` at delivery time is logged as `webhook.refused` and not sent; a callback to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/` from a key that allows that host is delivered
notes:
Decision to apply: require https for callbacks unless the resolved address is loopback, RFC 1918 or unique-local, so a hosted akou never sends a transcript across the internet in cleartext; the archive's TRANSCRIPTION_CALLBACK_URL follows the same rule (service-interface.md).
Owner decision from review (PR #33): delivery must connect to the exact address that passed the range check (no second DNS lookup between check and connect, so DNS rebinding cannot swap in a private address), while HTTPS still verifies the certificate and hostname against the callback URL's host (SNI = the hostname). Test: a resolver that answers a public address at check time and 127.0.0.1 at connect time must not reach 127.0.0.1.

title: SV-D2: Loopback by default, network by choice
description:
Owning doc: docs/ux/SERVER.md#2-decisions-this-reverses (SV-D2).

Rule 3, `Host` must be exactly `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>` ([guard.ts](../../src/main/api/guard.ts) lines 64 to 67): in server mode `Host` must equal `server.public_host` when set, or any host when `server.behind_proxy` is true. DNS rebinding does not apply to a keyed non-loopback listener, so this is a safe relaxation

From: Server mode needs a reachable port, and a proxied request carries the proxy's host name
